question: Are any of Pollux's 9 Mahler-subset pairs more alike in mean-normalised spacing than random same-size subsets of the Mahler table (FRANK-004 stage 0 + stage 1), read with a statistic that cannot see the sorted-rank identity the daemon reported?

kwargs._note: for each of the 9 SEED_PAIRS: a,b = daemon._load_subset(spec) UNCHANGED; record corr_raw, corr_norm, verdict; require equality with pollux_rescan_result.json Q2 to 4 dp (organ_execution_plan (a)); mismatch -> STOP, record against proposer
instrument-null reading of the daemon statistic on the 9 pairs (expected TAUTOLOGICAL; already measured on synthetic input in adapters_instrument_null.SYNTHETIC_NULL)

for each pair and each side: 5 halvings, 1000 draws, seed 20260911, alpha 0.05/9; pool = all MAHLER_TABLE M values; resolvable iff >= 4/5 halvings at p_lower < alpha. PRE-RUN FINDING: this control cannot pass for any iid continuous gap law (see pre_run_findings[0])
subset A vs expovariate(1) gaps of size n_b-1; void if p_lower < 0.05

stage 1, only for pairs marked resolvable in step 2; unmatched random-subset null AND M-range-matched null (pool restricted to [min(M_a,M_b), max(M_a,M_b)]); report d_observed, null median / 5th pct, p_lower, p_bonferroni(x9), verdict, and the step-0 ancestor verdict beside it
scipy ks_2samp D on every stage-1 pair must equal adapters ks_distance to 1e-9 (PARITY already PASS in adapters_resampling_null.PARITY.ks_distance_matches_scipy)
census of any Pollux state ledger that exists on the reachable tree (organ pollux.schemas.0 reads only; no ledger bytes were found on 2026-09-11)

positive.name: split-half
positive.rule: >= 4 of 5 halvings at p_lower < 0.05/9 per side
positive.pre_run_status: CANNOT PASS on iid continuous gaps (measured hit rate 0.0133 at alpha 0.00556, 0/30 resolvable); see pre_run_findings

repetition.name: seed repetition
repetition.rule: same seed -> identical null quantiles and p (adapters_resampling_null.REPETITION.same_seed_same_null PASS)

ancestor_parity.name: daemon replay
ancestor_parity.rule: corr_norm equal to pollux_rescan_result.json Q2 to 4 dp on all 9 pairs

kill_criteria: (1) step 0 fails to reproduce on-record corr_norm/verdicts -> NOT RUN; recorded against the proposer
(2) every pair fails the split-half control -> pollux_spacing_unresolvable on all 9 -> monster DEAD BEFORE RUN against the proposer (FIRES PRE-RUN, see pre_run_findings)
(3) any negative control p_lower < 0.05 -> that pair VOID (instrument reads Poisson spacing as coincidence)
(4) no resolvable pair reaches p_lower < 0.05/9 on all 5 seeds under the unmatched null -> Pollux hypothesis DEAD in its stated form
(5) a pair alive under the unmatched null but not under the M-matched null -> 'explained by M-range', hypothesis clause 'beyond what scale explains' fails for that pair
(6) stage-1 p at the floor 1/1001 on any seed -> report 'p <= 1/1001', never 0

expected_outputs.row_schema: per pair x seed: {pair, n_a, n_b, ks_distance, null_n, null_quantile, p_lower, p_bonferroni, split_half_p, negative_control_p, seed, verdict, ancestor_corr_norm, ancestor_verdict} (FRANK-004 organ 6 stats fields)

non_resurrection_argument.X1: no daemon process is started; daemon.py is imported for _load_subset and _mean_spacing_normalize only (pure functions), run_tick is never called
non_resurrection_argument.X2: charon/agents/pollux/state is never opened for writing; all writes go to <run_dir>
non_resurrection_argument.X3: no saved state is loaded; SEED_PAIRS is read as a constant
non_resurrection_argument.X4: no pair rotation, no CANDIDATE_POOL promotion, no new specs: the 9 SEED_PAIRS are fixed inputs
non_resurrection_argument.X5: no parameter is searched; seeds, alpha, n_draws are pre-registered constants
non_resurrection_argument.X6: inputs are fingerprinted here and re-fingerprinted at run time; the ancestor verdict is replayed on identical inputs
non_resurrection_argument.X7: the KS read is filed under NT-049 (NECROPOLIS ADAPTER); the ancestor read under NT-048/NT-010 (UNTRUSTED); RESULT.json keeps them in separate columns

pre_run_findings.title: Kill criterion (2) fires on synthetic data before any grave is read
pre_run_findings.measured: engine/necropolis/workshop/tests/run_controls.py::adapters_resampling_null.PERTURBATION.split_half_control_fails_at_alpha_rate_for_iid_continuous -- 30 tight-lognormal sequences (n=200) vs a uniform pool, 5 halvings each: hit rate 0.0133 at alpha 0.00556, 0/30 resolvable; 50 percent member overlap gave p_lower ~0.3
pre_run_findings.why: the two-sample KS statistic is distribution-free under 'same distribution'; the random-subset null at the half sizes IS a same-distribution null for any iid continuous gap law, so P(p_lower < alpha) = alpha regardless of n or shape. The lower tail can only see an IDENTICAL gap multiset (D ~ 0), measured in adapters_resampling_null.SYNTHETIC_SIGNAL.identical_gap_multiset_is_seen
pre_run_findings.input_characterisation: MAHLER_TABLE: 8625 rows, 8497 distinct M, 143 rows in tied groups (1.7 percent); largest ties M=1.0 (29), 1.17628081826 (21), 1.324717957245 (16) -- ties are too sparse to produce identical gap multisets between degree subsets
pre_run_findings.consequence: as written, FRANK-004 stage 0 marks all 9 pairs pollux_spacing_unresolvable and the monster is DEAD BEFORE RUN against the proposer. This is a finding about the DESIGN (the proposer's split-half rule, cleric_gate note (iv)), not about Pollux's hypothesis
pre_run_findings.recommendation: before HITL approval, refile the read in the UPPER tail (do selected subsets DIFFER from random subsets more than random subsets differ from each other; p_upper), or with a location/scale-sensitive distance whose null is not distribution-free under 'same law' (Anderson-Darling on gaps; energy distance), and replace the split-half positive control with a planted-shift control whose pass rate is not pinned at alpha. Until then this plan is a record of why the monster cannot run, not a request to run it
